connection-admission.reason: wait_for_admission in src/control.rs polls GET /v1/operations/{id} (the OperationResource id, else the id at the end of links.self): ready, no operation and 404 are admitted, failed and timed_out are ThalovantError::AdmissionFailed with the operation's error_code, requested/committed/applied keep polling, a 5xx is ridden out, another API refusal is AdmissionFailed with its status and problem, and the deadline (each GET bounded by it) is ThalovantError::AdmissionTimeout, for which is_timeout() and is_connection_error() in src/errors.rs are both true -- the runner asserts both. An absolute links.self on another origin than the API's is ThalovantError::Api and never fetched. A 429 is ridden out too, waiting the problem's retry_after_seconds (top level or inside a detail object) or the poll interval when that is longer, and a 429 asking for longer than is left is AdmissionTimeout at once; an unreachable API passes through unchanged. Every duration in the vectors is whole milliseconds, so the recorder keeps its strict whole-number rule. tests/home_link.rs serves each case's exchanges from a loopback HTTP peer, in order, through the real ControlPlane path, checks every request's method, path, body or body subset, If-Match and Authorization, requires every exchange to be used, and records what it produced through tests/common/mod.rs -- hashed beside it because it controls canonicalisation -- before asserting.

The runner asserts every refusal it classifies is still ApiResponse. tests/home_link.rs serves each case's exchanges from a loopback HTTP peer, in order, through the real ControlPlane path, checks every request's method, path, body or body subset, If-Match and Authorization, requires every exchange to be used, and records what it produced through tests/common/mod.rs -- hashed beside it because it controls canonicalisation -- before asserting.

device-login.reason: begin_device_login, poll_device_login (one POST /v1/auth/device/token, returning the ApiToken or ThalovantError::DeviceLoginPending with the interval -- lengthened by five seconds for good per device code, kept in the control plane's private device_intervals -- DeviceLoginExpired or DeviceLoginDenied, each with the status and boxed problem) and revoke_api_token live in src/control.rs; revoking the token in use treats the API's 401 as revoked and forgets it, revoking again sends nothing until the next sign-in (a private flag every sign-in clears), and every sign-in sets token_id from its own answer; the variants and their status_code/api_problem answers in src/errors.rs. home-link.reason: src/home.rs holds HOME_REQUEST/HOME_RESPONSE, HOME_REQUEST_TIMEOUT, RESPONSE_TYPES and ERROR_CODES (asserted equal to the vector file's lists), HomeRequest, HomeAnswer, home_response, plain_speech (strip_ssml, then character references decoded as html.unescape does -- every numeric reference, and HTML 4's named ones, ' and the upper-case spellings, in src/home/entities.rs, generated from Python's html.entities; any other HTML5 name is left as written -- then Unicode whitespace collapsed as str.isspace sees it), answer_home_request (handler bounded by tokio::time::timeout; an error or panic is failed_to_handle, elapsed is timeout, outside the lists is unknown, exactly one reply) and answer_home_requests. reply_context is in src/events.rs, Client::reply in src/client.rs, which replies from Event::context, the context exactly as the hub sent it. src/session.rs adds per-type handlers bound on every client the session builds, a state callback, connect() with the 0.75 s settle window, run() with the ladder, drop detection and the 600 s refusal grace, and for_identity; src/transport.rs remembers whether the last WSS close was a refusal (no status, 1000, 1005, 1008, or a 401/403 upgrade) and wakes waiters when a link stops. refusal.reason: refusal_belongs_to_ask() and failure_error() live in src/refusal.rs with their vector suite colocated, as this SDK's private unit suites are, so the module is recorded as test evidence beside the errors and transport it rests on; collect_ask_reply() in client.rs applies the rule with the transport's count of asks, queries and fire-and-forget utterances inside the shared grace window -- recorded once connected and immediately before the publish, and kept when the publish errors, since emit_bus over HTTP can fail after the hub holds the frame. runtime.reason: Applicable public behavior is implemented and exercised by the named regression suites and shared fixtures. Rust unit tests are colocated with their implementation; complete tested modules are recorded as test evidence and exports/delegates as implementation evidence. HiveMind #251/#252 only changes the Python upstream client dispatcher; this consumer uses native single-dispatch transports (MCP delegates to the Node SDK), or caller-owned frame parsing in embedded C. No Python HiveMind bus dependency or slave-protocol reinjection exists here. Python now requires fixed upstream 1.1.9a1 and removes its identity-based suppression; equal independent native frames remain distinct. Reply claim metadata follows the Python string-ID contract, with first-seen ordering, case-sensitive fallback stages and legacy unstamped success. Invalid non-string stamps are ignored. Embedded C exposes bounded extraction and claim classification while its caller retains ordered IDs.
